description: What changes month by month on the Antarctic Peninsula between November and March: sea ice, daylight, penguin breeding stages, whale sightings and air temperature. Every row is sourced.
caption: Antarctic Peninsula and South Shetland Islands, November to March. Numbers in brackets refer to the sources below the chart.
legend: Daylight bar: share of 24 hours. Ice squares: relative ice level described by the sources (three = most). Temperatures are 30-season averages (1996–2025) we calculated from British Antarctic Survey station records; individual days vary widely. Where no source gives a month-specific figure, the cell says so.

notes.heading: How the season is defined
notes.html: IAATO, the tour operators' association, describes the Antarctic Peninsula season as the seven-month austral summer, from October to April. In the 2024-25 season, landings took place over about 162 days, from 22 October to 1 April. The chart covers November to March.

notes.heading: How the daylight figures were calculated
notes.html: Sunrise to sunset on the 15th of each month of the 2026-27 season, calculated with the NOAA solar calculator equations (sun's centre at 0.833° below the horizon, which allows for refraction). Twilight adds more usable light on top of these figures.

notes.heading: How the temperatures were calculated
notes.html: Arithmetic means of the monthly mean surface air temperatures for 1996 to 2025 published by the British Antarctic Survey's READER project, for Faraday/Vernadsky, Rothera, Esperanza and Bellingshausen stations. The British Antarctic Survey does not publish these averages in this form; we calculated them from its tables.
